citation.authors: Forsyth JE, Mistree D, Nash E, Angrish M et al

record.population: Turmeric root and powder samples from bazaars in 23 cities in India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal (2020 to 2021)
record.design: Laboratory survey of lead and chromium in 356 samples
record.finding: Fourteen per cent (51 samples) had lead above 2 micrograms per gram, and samples at 18 or more had lead-to-chromium ratios pointing to lead chromate added as a colouring. Lead levels exceeded 1,000 micrograms per gram in Patna (India), Karachi and Peshawar (Pakistan).
record.note: A product survey in South Asia, not a study of people. It matters because the spice is traded worldwide. It is a warning about loose spice from uncertain sources.
